title: North-star sprint ephemera — weekly OKR scratch
content:
Purpose: quick living page for my personal quarterly focus (north-star) and the micro-sprints that feed it. Not polished; this is where I jot hypotheses, friction, and small experiments.

CONTEXT / WHY
- 1-line north-star (quarter): ship two high-impact integrations that reduce customer latency by 30% on median tail for embedding-heavy endpoints and create a reproducible rollout checklist so I can hand off to SEs.
- Why this matters: reduces customer costs and error surface, frees SE time, aligns with product goal to lower unit economics.

OBJECTIVE (working)
- Objective Q1: Make inference integrations predictable (deploy + observe) so product teams can ship with confidence.

KEY RESULTS (hypotheses — draft)
- KR1: Reduce median embedding request P95 latency by 30% on two pilot customers (A/B baseline).
- KR2: Create an integration playbook + runbook and validate with 3 internal SE-led dry runs.
- KR3: Cut mean time-to-detect (MTTD) regressions for model rollouts from 18h -> 6h using alerts + smoke prompts.

WEEKLY SPRINT NOTES (current week — Mar 2–8, 2026)
- Monday: sketched integration playbook outline (sections: preflight, canary, load profile, rollback conditions). TODO: add exact SLIs and thresholds.
- Tuesday: paired with Ethan on canary traffic shaping. Action: add traffic-weights matrix to playbook (RD-2108).
- Wednesday: quick call with Maya — gated by observability gaps (tracing missing for token-level dropouts). Filed follow-up ticket: OBS-4402.
- Thursday: ran first dry-run on staging with SE sim; saw 1.2x higher tail under cold-cache — root cause likely missing KV cache warm-up.
- Friday: retro notes below + plan to prototype a warm-up shim.

RETRO — what worked / pain points
- Wins: playbook draft moves faster when I pair with SE; dry-run surfaced a single common failure mode (cache warm-up) which is straightforward.
- Pain: metrics surfaced too late — logging pipeline has ~30–45m lag for per-token traces. This blocks fast MTTD.
- Hypothesis: adding a small subset of low-latency telemetry (heartbeat events + sample traces sent to hot path) can reduce detection time to under 5 minutes.
- Risk: increased telemetry may increase cost for high-throughput customers. Need cost/benefit.

EXPERIMENTS / MICRO-PLANS (next 2 weeks)
- Experiment A: Implement warm-up shim (client-side small fill requests) — measure tail latency improvement. Owner: Juniper. Est effort: 2d.
- Experiment B: Prototype hot-path telemetry (sample 1% token events) and route to realtime alerting channel. Owner: Ethan. Est effort: 4d.
- Experiment C: Run 3 internal dry-runs with canary weights [1%, 5%, 20%] and grading checklist. Owner: Maya + Juniper. Est effort: ongoing.

PERSONAL HABIT TRACKER (to support throughput)
- Focus slots: 2x 90m deep work blocks on Mon/Wed/Thu.
- Weekly writeup: ship a 300–500 word recap on Friday (keeps momentum).
- Friction: context-switching from meetings; try 1 day meeting-free.

MEASUREMENT NOTES / DATA SOURCES
- Baselines: use the staging perf suite (tag: staging/2026-02-23) for median/P95 baseline.
- Alerts: connect playbook to alert policy: latency.P95 > baseline*1.25 -> notify #oncall-se + page.
- Validation: ask SE to confirm acceptance criteria post-dry-run (checkbox in playbook).

OPEN QUESTIONS / DECISIONS NEEDED
- How much telemetry sampling is acceptable before customers push back? (bring to weekly product sync).
- Approval needed from infra for hot-path pipeline change (OBS-4402 blockers).
- Should we include a forced warm-up step in the SDK or keep it as an integration step? Pro: SDK makes it easier; Con: impacts client startup cost.

ACTION ITEMS (short)
- [ ] Draft playbook SLI section with actual metrics and thresholds (due Mar 10).
- [ ] Create warm-up shim PoC and benchmark on staging (due Mar 12).
- [ ] Sync with infra on OBS-4402 and get cost estimate for hot-path telemetry (due Mar 11).
- [ ] Schedule 3 dry-runs with SE volunteers and record outcomes checklist (start Mar 15).

NOTES / LINKS / CONTEXT CLIPPINGS
- Slack threads: #se-infra (thread: "canary-weights-3/2"), #product-integrations.
- Related ticket: RD-2108 (integration playbook epic), OBS-4402 (tracing lag).
- Reference: Confluence playbook template (linked above) — strip the org-level jargon and keep actionable checkboxes.

FREEFORM / THINGS TO REMEMBER (notes to self)
- Keep the playbook consumable by an individual SE (not a team). Single-sentence acceptance criteria are gold.
- If warm-up shim reduces tail substantially, bundle as optional SDK helper with clear opt-out.
- When handing over, include a 15m demo video + checklist; that materially increases adoption.

END — quick log entry (Mar 5): felt momentum today; small wins compound. Next week: focus on low-latency visibility and the warm-up shim.
